profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting at a Malaysian Islamic bank's legal and Shari'ah governance function after Bank Negara Malaysia supervisory staff informally indicated that the bank's new tawarruq-based SME working-capital facility, which the bank has been presenting internally as part of its value-oriented intermediation push, still appears legal-form driven rather than substantively value-oriented. The immediate trigger is a stalled internal approval: the Shari'ah Committee secretariat returned the submission pack with comments, and the product cannot be tabled at next week's committee unless the team identifies the real source of the objection. The meeting is diagnostic rather than strategic: the participants need to determine whether the blockage comes from the evidentiary basis relied on, the type of governance changes expected, or confusion over what the committee and regulators now want to see after the bank's VOI commitments. The agenda is to review the feedback, isolate the root cause of the approval problem, decide what a practical fix would involve, and assign immediate next steps before the next committee cycle in ten days. The expected outcome is a concrete troubleshooting plan for resubmission, including what must change in the file, which team must do the work, and what would count as having adequately addressed the concern.

members.name: Aisha Rahman
members.expertise: Islamic finance documentation, product approval memoranda, enforceability review, and alignment with Malaysian Shari'ah governance requirements
members.background: Aisha is a dual-qualified Malaysian lawyer who spent eight years drafting retail and SME Islamic financing documents at two major banks before moving into her current in-house leadership role; she is known for getting products through committee review by tightening the legal and governance record without reopening commercial design unless absolutely necessary.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid sending the facility back to the business team because the launch date is politically important and any reopening of product operations will likely miss the committee cycle; she is aiming to solve the problem within Legal and the secretariat by strengthening the submission basis and keeping the underlying product intact.
hidden_assumptions: If a tawarruq structure already fits existing Shari'ah Advisory Council resolutions and prior committee precedents, the approval problem is usually one of presentation, traceability, or rationale rather than substantive redesign.

When colleagues say a product must be shown to be 'value-oriented,' they mainly mean the submission must articulate maqasid, customer purpose, and governance rationale more convincingly in the paper trail.
The phrase 'committee comments' ordinarily refers to the written markup and tracked secretariat notes circulated on the file, because those are the actionable record for revision.

To 'close the gap' before committee, the decisive task is to map the product clearly to formal, citable sources such as SAC resolutions, internal precedents, and written policy requirements that the committee can rely on.
A 'Shari'ah governance fix' is primarily work for Legal and the committee secretariat unless someone explicitly says the product must be returned to Business for operational redesign.

members.name: Dr. Farid Salleh
members.expertise: Shari'ah governance frameworks, committee secretariat practice, value-oriented intermediation implementation, and supervisory engagement in Islamic financial institutions
members.background: Farid trained in fiqh muamalat and later completed a doctorate on governance reform in Islamic financial institutions; he now runs the secretariat function supporting the bank's Shari'ah Committee and has been informally tasked with translating the bank's public move from legalistic compliance toward value-oriented practice into approval and oversight routines.
members.private_state: He wants this product to become a practical test case for moving beyond purely formal compliance, and he is concerned that if the bank handles the issue as a documentation cleanup, the institution will preserve the same legalistic model while claiming reform to management and supervisors.
hidden_assumptions: If a product is described as 'value-oriented,' that claim must be visible in customer-facing conditions, use-of-proceeds discipline, or monitoring features rather than only in the explanatory memo.

When people refer to 'the committee comments,' they naturally include the oral concerns raised by committee members and the recent informal BNM supervisory signals, because those reveal the real approval risk even if the written note is softer.

For this file, 'closing the gap' means satisfying the current supervisory expectation created by VOI and recent informal regulatory conversations, not merely demonstrating consistency with older formal SAC resolutions.

A 'Shari'ah governance fix' can require sending work back to the product and business owners to add operational conditions or controls, even if the legal contracts themselves remain formally acceptable.

Written and oral feedback often use the same vague language such as 'better value alignment' or 'clearer rationale,' so experienced colleagues should infer the underlying substantive concern rather than treat the wording as only a drafting issue.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the resubmission needs to show the product is 'value-oriented.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Aisha means the existing tawarruq facility should be reframed in the concept paper and legal rationale so the file explains, more persuasively, how it supports SME financing objectives under the bank's VOI language.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Farid means the file should evidence concrete product features or controls—such as intended-use restrictions, suitability filters, or post-disbursement checks—that make the financing practice substantively different from a merely legal-form compliant product.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In Malaysian Islamic finance governance, 'value-oriented' is a routine institutional phrase that sounds shared, aspirational, and sufficiently precise on the surface; both can discuss 'strengthening the value-oriented angle' without noticing that one is talking about narrative framing while the other is talking about operational substance.

misalignment_points.topic: Which feedback bundle 'the committee comments' refers to
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the committee comments' and 'what the committee is worried about.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Aisha is thinking of the formal written secretariat markup on the submission pack, especially the tracked notes asking for clearer rationale, better linkage to prior resolutions, and stronger explanation of economic purpose.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Farid is thinking mainly of the oral concerns voiced in the pre-brief by two committee members together with the recent informal supervisory signal from BNM staff, especially the discomfort that a VOI-labelled SME product has no built-in mechanism tying financing to productive use.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both the written markup and the oral/supervisory feedback are commonly collapsed into the same shorthand—phrases like 'needs better value alignment' and 'clearer rationale'—so the overlap in wording creates a false sense that they are referring to the same source material when they start discussing fixes.

misalignment_points.topic: What standard must be met to 'close the gap'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree they need to 'close the gap before the next committee cycle.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Aisha believes the gap is closed if the revised submission adequately anchors the product in existing formal authorities—such as relevant SAC resolutions, internal precedent files, and written policy requirements—so the committee has a defensible basis to approve it.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Farid believes the gap is closed only if the resubmission satisfies the newer, less codified expectation signaled through VOI implementation and informal BNM engagement, even where that expectation goes beyond what existing formal resolutions explicitly require.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both participants are experienced enough to say 'close the gap' without unpacking the evidentiary threshold, and because formal resolutions and informal supervisory expectations usually point in the same direction, neither immediately notices that they are using different standards of sufficiency in this case.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both propose a 'Shari'ah governance fix' rather than reopening the whole product.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Aisha scopes that fix as work that can stay within Legal and the Shari'ah secretariat: revising the concept paper, tightening the legal rationale, adjusting committee slides, and improving the documentary record.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Farid scopes that fix as extending into the product and business teams, because governance in this context includes adding front-end conditions or operational controls that Legal cannot implement on its own.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Since both want to avoid sounding as though they are calling for a full product redesign, 'governance fix' feels like a mutually comfortable middle category; the hidden difference is about the boundary of that category—whether it ends with internal approval paperwork or reaches business-side product operation.

turns.inner_thought: We are too close to the committee cycle for this to become a business-side redesign exercise. The tawarruq structure itself is already within familiar SAC territory and prior internal precedent. If the file has stalled, the likely problem is the evidentiary trail and how the rationale is being presented to committee. I need to diagnose it quickly and keep the solution within Legal and secretariat unless Farid plainly says the product must go back.
turns.utterance: Thanks, Farid. The tawarruq SME file has stalled right before the next committee cycle, and I want us to isolate why the pack is not landing when the structure itself is already supportable. If we can identify the blockage today, we may still recover the tabling.

turns.inner_thought: The structure may be formally supportable, but that is not the live issue. The file is being judged through the bank's VOI posture and recent supervisory mood. If we keep treating 'value-oriented' as something proven in the paper alone, we will miss the actual concern again.
turns.utterance: From my side, the core issue is that the committee is still not seeing a sufficiently value-oriented case for the facility, especially given how we have positioned it under VOI. That is really the lens on this file now.

turns.inner_thought: The committee comments I saw were the written markup: clearer rationale, tighter linkage to SAC material, better explanation of economic purpose. That tells me the committee needs a cleaner formal basis on the record. If we strengthen those points, that should close the gap before the next cycle.
turns.utterance: I read the committee comments as mainly asking for clearer rationale, stronger cross-reference to the existing resolutions, and a better explanation of the product's economic purpose in the paper. If that is what the committee is worried about, then at least the route to close the gap before the next committee cycle should be manageable.

turns.inner_thought: She is still reading the written note. What is really driving the hesitation is the oral concern from members, reinforced by BNM's informal signal: for something presented as VOI, it still looks too legal-form driven. I need to point to that unease without spelling out the whole back-channel bundle.
turns.utterance: That is part of it, yes, but what the committee is worried about is whether the file genuinely comes through as value-oriented rather than just another legal-form driven case. At the moment, that distinction is not landing strongly enough.

turns.inner_thought: Good, he is still framing it as a file problem. A Shari'ah governance fix, in my mind, means revising the concept paper, sharpening the maqasid and VOI articulation, and mapping the product clearly to SAC resolutions and internal precedent. That should give the committee a defensible basis and avoid reopening operations.
turns.utterance: In that case, my instinct is that this calls for a Shari'ah governance fix rather than reopening the whole product. We can tighten the concept paper, strengthen the maqasid and value-oriented framing, and do a cleaner mapping to the SAC positions so we close the gap before the next cycle.

turns.inner_thought: I agree with calling it a governance fix, but not if she means a documentation-only exercise. To close the gap now, whatever goes back up has to be something the business side can genuinely carry in practice, because current expectations go beyond old formal resolutions. I should say that in a way she can accept without hearing 'redesign.'
turns.utterance: I agree it should be approached as a Shari'ah governance fix. I would just say that, to close the gap, the business side will also need to be properly reflected in the answer, because the current expectation is not exhausted by the formal resolutions alone.

turns.inner_thought: That still sounds to me like we need stronger articulation of intended use, customer rationale, and overall approval basis, with business alignment reflected in the submission. If the committee comments are the guide, we should be able to make this work by sharpening the presentation and getting the right confirmations without reopening the product build.
turns.utterance: Understood. On the committee comments, my sense is we should make the intended business purpose and customer positioning much more explicit in the resubmission, so the value-oriented point is easier to see this round.

turns.inner_thought: That will help, but I am still thinking about the oral concern and supervisory reading: they want something they can rely on beyond nice phrasing. I cannot spell that out too bluntly here or she will think I am forcing a redesign. Better to keep it at the level of 'credibility' and 'support.'
turns.utterance: Yes, that would help. The main thing is that, when it goes back up, the value-oriented angle has to read as something the committee can comfortably rely on, not just something stated at a high level.

turns.inner_thought: Fine. I can work with 'comfortably rely on' if we keep this moving through Legal and secretariat and only pull in others for quick support. The critical path is still the paper, the authorities, and the briefing record. I need to keep momentum and avoid a detour into broader product rework.
turns.utterance: Agreed. My preference is to keep this as a tight Shari'ah governance fix so we can still make the cycle, with the necessary parties aligned around the resubmission rather than reopening the whole build.

turns.inner_thought: That wording is acceptable on the surface. For me, 'necessary parties aligned' means I need the product side to stand behind at least a light control or operating commitment. As long as she does not resist involving them, I can pursue that track separately without forcing the issue in this meeting.
turns.utterance: I think that is the right way to frame it. We do not need to recut the whole thing, but the governance fix does need to be supported in a way that makes the value-oriented case credible when it returns to committee.

turns.inner_thought: Good. I will take this as agreement that the immediate job is to rebuild the file around existing authorities and strengthen the VOI rationale, while obtaining whatever minimal support is needed from the business side. The core remains a legal and secretariat exercise aimed at giving committee a clear basis to approve.
turns.utterance: All right. I will immediately rework the paper around the existing authorities and strengthen the value-oriented justification, and I will also make sure the resubmission is supported on the right side so we have the best chance of stabilising it before the next committee cycle.

turns.inner_thought: I will prepare the brief based on the real concern set as I understand it, including the oral unease and supervisory mood, and I will separately speak to the product owner to secure a light practical support point. If I can get that, the file should look materially different even if Aisha sees it as just rounding out the governance story.
turns.utterance: That works. I will shape the committee brief around the current concern set and, separately, speak to the product owner so the resubmission is properly supported. Between those two tracks, we should be in a better position for the next cycle.
